URL: https://zapier.com/blog/sms-messaging-automation
How to automate your text messages with Zapier
Whether you're engaging leads, following up on form submissions, or sending critical reminders, text messages cut through the noise of crowded email inboxes and provide an immediate, reliable way to reach your audience. But manually managing these messages isn't a smart plan if you want to scale your business. That's where automation comes in.
By pairing SMS tools with Zapier, you can seamlessly integrate texting into your workflows so the right messages reach the right people at the right time. From sending automated reminders for calendar events to instantly following up with leads, automating SMS allows you to deliver critical updates while saving time and reducing manual work.
You can set all of this up from the AI tool you already use. Add Zapier to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor, tell your agent which text should go out and when, and it builds the automation. Zapier then keeps sending those texts after the chat is closed. And if you'd rather build in Zapier itself, you can do that too.
Whether you're managing customer relationships, team coordination, or personal productivity, Zaps will help you stay organized, responsive, and on top of what matters most. Let's dive into how SMS automation can transform your communication strategy and keep you one step ahead.
Build automations from wherever you work. Describe the outcome you want, and Zapier connects your tools, runs the steps, and stays on the job after you close the chat. Combine AI with reliable, deterministic automation across 9,000+ apps. Get started for free.
Build SMS automations from your AI assistant
SMS automations to ask your agent to build
SMS automation is the use of software to send text messages automatically. It can mean sending messages based on a trigger, like a form submission, a calendar event, or a new row in a spreadsheet sets it off, or it can fire on a schedule you choose. You set the rule once, and the right text goes to the right person without anyone typing it out.
Customers and leads get confirmations, reminders, and follow-ups, while your own team gets alerts about urgent emails, new orders, or system updates, so nothing waits on someone remembering to hit send.
Build SMS automations from your AI assistant
Here's how it works when you start from your AI tool:
Connect Zapier with your AI tool. Add Zapier to your AI assistant as a connector or a custom MCP server, and connect the apps you use, like Twilio, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Google Calendar. You connect once, and the same connections work from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any AI tool you like.
Describe the text you want sent. Tell your agent what should trigger it, who gets it, and what it says: "When someone books a call on Calendly, text them a confirmation with the time and the join link."
Your agent turns it into a Zap. A Zap is an automated workflow that runs on its own. Your agent drafts it, deploys it to Zapier, and shows you what it built before anything goes live.
Zapier sends the texts. The Zap starts the moment the booking, form submission, or new row shows up, and it keeps going whether or not your laptop is open.
Because Zapier connects to 9,000+ apps, your texts can be triggered by almost anything in your stack, from a CRM to a custom app.
You could ask your AI tool to text people on its own. Building the automation on Zapier gets you a few things chat alone can't:
It starts when something happens. A scheduled task inside an AI tool runs at a set time, whether or not anything came up. A Zap can start on a schedule, or it can start when a registration comes in, a lead is created, or an appointment is booked, so the confirmation lands while the person is still paying attention.
It reaches your whole stack. Zapier connects to 9,000+ apps, so a text can be triggered by your calendar, your CRM, your spreadsheets, your help desk, or a webhook from a tool Zapier doesn't have a built-in connection to. Chat connectors tend to stop at the most popular apps.
It runs the same way every time. A reminder Zap sends the same text at the same point before every appointment, on a quiet Tuesday or a packed Friday. Zaps use AI only for steps that need judgment, like deciding whether an inbound reply is a complaint or a question, and run everything else as plain steps. Zapier calls this fluid determinism: AI where the work needs judgment, regular steps everywhere else.
It fixes itself. If your Twilio connection expires or a column in your Google Sheet gets renamed, your reminders shouldn't quietly stop and leave people uninformed. Zapier logs every run, finds the problem when something breaks, and proposes a fix you can approve, or lets Zapier apply fixes on its own. Over time it can also turn repeated AI steps into regular ones, so your Zaps get cheaper and steadier the longer they run.
Your agent gets access, not your keys. Zapier manages the connections to Twilio, WhatsApp, Gmail, and the rest, so you never paste API keys or auth tokens into a chat. Switch from Claude to ChatGPT, or try a new AI tool, and your connections stay put. Everything you build, from any AI tool, shows up in one place in Zapier.
SMS automations to ask your agent to build
Not sure where to start? Try one of these prompts in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor with Zapier connected.
Send shipping updates. "When an order ships in Shopify, text the customer their tracking link."
Alert the on-call person. "When a Zendesk ticket is marked high priority, text whoever is on call the subject line and a link to the ticket."
Nudge failed payments. "When a payment fails in Stripe, text the customer a friendly note with a link to update their card."
Sort replies by what they say. "When a customer replies to my Twilio number, have AI decide whether it's a question, a complaint, or a thank-you, and post it in the matching Slack channel." This is a Zap that uses AI only where judgment is needed: reading the reply is the AI step, and the Slack post is a regular step.
Start the week with your due dates. "Every Friday at 4 p.m., text me the tasks in Asana that are due next week."
Would you rather start from a template? The Zaps below are pre-made for common text message automations. Click "Try it" on any of them to open it in Zapier and set it up there. If you'd rather have your agent build the automation for you, use one of the prompts above instead.

As soon as someone submits their details, you can automatically trigger an SMS confirmation to their phone using tools like SMS by Zapier , WhatsApp , or Twilio . Contact forms provide an accessible, user-friendly way to get info from potential clients and customers. They're useful, but if their responses remain stuck in your form submission tool, powerful information can quickly go to waste.
If you connect forms to your other apps, you can turn these entries into business growth drivers.
You can set that up from the AI assistant you already use: add Zapier to it, tell your agent where each submission should go, and it builds the automation. Zapier keeps it running after the chat is closed, getting the details from your form tool into the places where you connect with customers and plan your work. And if you'd rather build in Zapier itself, you can do that too.
Build automations from wherever you work. Describe the outcome you want, and Zapier connects your tools, runs the steps, and stays on the job after you close the chat. Combine AI with reliable, deterministic automation across 9,000+ apps. Get started for free.
Build contact form automations from your AI assistant
Contact form automations to ask your agent to build
Contact form automation with Zap templates
Contact form automation is using software to handle what happens after someone hits submit: replying to them, logging them in your CRM, alerting your team, and filing their message where it belongs, without anyone copying details by hand.
Instead of checking your form tool's inbox, each submission kicks off a chain of steps, like an instant reply, a new contact in your CRM, a Slack alert, or a row in a spreadsheet. The same form can bring in a sales lead, a support request, and product feedback, and each one ends up in the right tool.
Build contact form automations from your AI assistant
Here's how a new contact form submission goes wherever you need it, automatically:
Connect Zapier with your AI tool. Add Zapier to your AI assistant as a connector or a custom MCP server, and connect the apps you use, like Typeform, Google Forms, Gmail, and HubSpot. You connect once, and the same connections work from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any AI tool you like.
Describe the job. Tell your agent what should happen in plain language: "When someone fills out my contact form, email them a thank-you, add them to HubSpot, and post their message in #leads in Slack."
Your agent turns it into a Zap. A Zap is an automated workflow that runs on its own. Your agent drafts it, deploys it to Zapier, and shows you what it built.
Zapier runs it. The Zap starts the moment a submission comes in, so the reply goes out while the lead is still thinking about you, and it keeps running whether or not your laptop is open.
Because Zapier connects to 9,000+ apps, the same submission can reach whichever form tool, CRM, and chat app your team uses.
Your AI assistant can read a form submission and draft a reply, but only while you're chatting with it. Building on Zapier adds a few things chat alone can't:
It starts when something happens. Scheduled tasks inside an AI tool run at set times, whether or not anyone filled out your form. A Zap starts the moment a submission lands, so a new lead hears back in seconds instead of whenever the next check happens.
It reaches your whole stack. Zapier connects to 9,000+ apps. That means it can turn a Typeform response into a lead in Salesforce or a Gravity Forms entry into a Trello card—whatever apps you use.
It runs the same way every time. Every submission gets the same thank-you, the same CRM record, and the same Slack alert, at 2 a.m. or 2 p.m. Zaps use AI only for steps that need judgment, like telling a sales inquiry from a support request, and run everything else as regular steps, which are faster and cheaper.
It fixes itself. If your Typeform connection expires or a HubSpot field gets renamed, submissions could pile up unanswered. Zapier finds the problem and proposes a fix you can approve, or applies fixes on its own if you let it. Repeated AI steps, like sorting inquiries by type, can also become regular steps over time.
Your agent gets access, not your keys. Zapier manages the logins to your form tool, inbox, and CRM, so you never paste passwords or API keys into a chat. Switch AI tools and your connections stay put, and every Zap you build, from any AI tool, shows up in one place in Zapier.
You could instead have your agent write a script that checks your form for new entries, and the first version will likely work. But the script needs somewhere to run, a way to learn about new submissions, and someone to keep it alive. And it stops quietly when a login expires or the form tool changes its API. With Zapier, your agent builds the Zap, and Zapier hosts it, runs it from real triggers (a form submission, a webhook, or a schedule), and keeps your connections working.

Reply right away and loop in the team. "When someone submits my website contact form, email them a thank-you that mentions what they asked about, and post the details in #leads in Slack."
Route each message by what it needs. "When a contact form comes in, decide whether it's a sales inquiry, a support request, or feedback. Add sales inquiries to HubSpot, create a Zendesk ticket for support requests, and save feedback to a Google Sheet." This is a good example of using AI only where judgment is needed: sorting the message is the AI step, and the CRM record, ticket, and spreadsheet row are regular steps.
Book the meeting. "When a Typeform response marks the lead as high priority, draft a Gmail message with my scheduling link and add a reminder to Google Calendar to follow up in two days."
Keep your CRM clean. "When a form entry arrives with an email that's already in Salesforce, update that contact instead of creating a duplicate."
Get a weekly read on what people are saying. "Every Friday at 4 p.m., summarize this week's contact form submissions by topic and email me the summary."
